newsitem.title: USA: Bradys ends higher, players cast eyes towards Fed.
newsitem.headline: Bradys ends higher, players cast eyes towards Fed.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices ended higher with spreads seen tighter across the Brady spectrum as players cast a watchful eye towards Tuesday's meeting of U.S. monetary policy makers, dealers said.

"The market rallied today. The tone in light trading is a positive one being that the market has already discounted a small move by the Fed," said Thomas Trebat, head of emerging market research at Citicorp Securities.
The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the U.S. Federal Reserve Board's policy-setting arm, is scheduled to meet to vote on monetary policy.
In a Reuter poll, 34 out of 48 economists expect the Fed to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent, at Tuesday's FOMC meeting.

"There was no particular news driving the market today," said one Brady trader. "In general, people seem to be more comfortable with the backdrop here...rates likely to go up 25 basis points tomorrow will lift a lot of uncertainty."

"Once we get that (rate hike) we're likely to have a little pop in prices just a relief rally of sorts," the trader said. "From there...our market will be taking cues from Treasuries and from what our clients do."
Dealers said activity on the buyside had been relatively quiet recently. However, as holders of Brady debt remained comfortable, a small rally was sustained the last couple of days.
While a 1/4 point rate hike is pretty much built into the market, underlying concerns over whether or not this move will be the first in a series by the Fed, is now the key concern.

"To some extent our market may not have priced in future hikes, but the Treasury market certainly has," a trader said. "If you look at Fed Funds futures for the next six-to-nine months, you'll see that...a 75 basis point tightening has been priced in, including tomorrow's impending hike, by the end of the year.
"Interestingly enough, the Treasury market has built in a nice concession for future hikes," he said. "Has our market? I would say partially, but not fully."
Among latin credits, Mexico Pars and Discounts were the key gainers on the day, rising 3/4 to trade at 73-1/2 bid, 89-5/8 bid, respectively.
"In Mexico, you have the strong local market and a strong peso keeping Bradys very well bid," another trader said.
Among other issuers faring well, were Venezuela Pars and Venezuela DCBS, which also traded up 3/8 to 73-1/4 bid and 87-1/2 bid, respectively.
Brazil "C" bonds also gained 1/2 to a 77-5/8 bid.
Argentina PARs were unchanged at 65 bid.

Looking ahead, Citicorp's Trebat said: "Opinion is mixed as to where we go from here, but my feeling is that the benefit will be felt more by shorter duration instruments such as the Venezuelan Dcbs, Argentine Frbs and Brazilian EIs, among others."
Venezuelan Dcbs were up 3/8 at 87-3/4 bid, Argentine Frbs gained 5/8 to 90-7/8 bid and Brazilian EIs ended a 1/4 higher at 89-7/8 bid.
Trebat expects those instruments to do reasonably well, not only because they lower Treasury risk, but also because they reflect good fundamentals in those various Latin American countries.
"We had a little of that reaction today," Trebat added.
Among other issues, Bulgaria IAB were up 1/8 to 60-1/2 bid, while Russian VN US$ fell 3/8 to 81-3/8 bid.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond closed up 17/32 at 96-8/32 to yield 6.92 percent.
